cost_ranges.note: SECONDARY SOURCE, DERIVED: CHOICE (prices from SolarQuotes partners) lists 10 kWh storage at AUD 7,000-11,000 installed after the federal rebate, and prints the 2026 rebate as AUD 272 per kWh (6.8 STC x about AUD 40). The calculator deducts the rebate itself, so the row is the before-rebate price: 7,000 + 2,720 = 9,720 (low); 11,000 + 2,720 = 13,720 (high); likely = midpoint 11,720 (derived, not published). Includes installation and GST. Real quotes vary with brand, inverter and installer. Not a quote.
cost_ranges.unit: AUD per battery system (10 kWh usable), BEFORE the federal rebate, incl. GST

cost_ranges.note: SECONDARY SOURCE (SolarQuotes, a lead-generation site, last updated 12 Oct 2026): typical fully installed prices buyers reported paying, 5 kW AUD 5,000-7,500; 6.6 kW 6,000-9,000; 8 kW 7,500-11,000; 10 kW 9,000-12,000. low = 10 kW low end 9,000 / 10,000 W = 0.90; likely = the page's rule of thumb of about AUD 1,000 per kW = 1.00; high = 5 kW high end 7,500 / 5,000 W = 1.50. The page does not state whether the STC discount is deducted or whether GST is included; treated as the price the buyer pays (after STCs, incl. GST). The 2026 STC discount shrinks every 1 January (deeming period 5 years in 2026, 4 in 2027), which is not modelled. Not a quote.
cost_ranges.unit: AUD per watt DC (after the point-of-sale STC discount, incl. GST)

export_policy_rates.note: IPART all-day benchmark 3.4 to 6.5 cents per kWh, 2026-27; likely = (3.4 + 6.5) / 2 = 4.95 (derived midpoint). Held flat over time.

export_policies.name: New South Wales: IPART all-day benchmark (2026-27)
export_policies.note: IPART benchmark range 3.4 to 6.5 cents per kWh for 2026-27, the range retailers are expected to price against (not a guaranteed rate). The likely value is the midpoint of the published range. Time-of-day benchmarks are higher in the evening (about 17 to 33 cents depending on the network) but are not modelled.

export_policies.name: Western Australia, Synergy: buyback outside 3 pm to 9 pm
export_policies.note: Synergy DEBS pays 2 cents per kWh for exports outside 3 pm to 9 pm (midday solar exports fall here) and 10 cents from 3 pm to 9 pm; only the 2 cent rate is modelled. Rates shown are those published as at 1 July 2024: the WA page was last updated in December 2024 and 2026-27 rates are not confirmed.

incentives.eligibility_note: Batteries certified for compliance from 1 May 2026, installed with solar, on the Clean Energy Council approved list; size tiers 100% / 60% / 15% of the factor for 0-14 / >14-28 / >28-50 usable kWh.
incentives.name: Cheaper Home Batteries Program (STC factor 6.8)
incentives.note: AUD per usable kWh = STC factor 6.8 x STC price: likely 39.62 x 6.8 = 269.42 (spot, CER, 15 May 2026), high 40 x 6.8 = 272.00 (Clearing House price), low = likely x 0.9 (10% admin fee, CHOICE, SECONDARY). Paid as a point-of-sale discount. State rebates and VPP incentives are not included.

incentives.eligibility_note: Batteries certified for compliance from 1 January 2027; same size tiers.
incentives.name: Cheaper Home Batteries Program (STC factor 5.7)
incentives.note: AUD per usable kWh = STC factor 5.7 x STC price: likely 39.62 x 5.7 = 225.83 (spot, CER, 15 May 2026), high 40 x 5.7 = 228.00, low = likely x 0.9 (10% admin fee, CHOICE, SECONDARY). The step down from 6.8 to 5.7 on 1 January 2027 is the Clean Energy Regulator schedule (reg 20(8)); the STC price in 2027 is not known.

markets.display_round_rationale: Assumption: round money to the nearest AUD 50 so that small homes (savings of a few hundred dollars a year) are not rounded to the nearest AUD 100.
markets.name: Australia
markets.vat_note: Australian prices are quoted including GST; cost rows are tax-inclusive (includes_tax = true), so no GST schedule is needed and markets.vat_rate stays null.

model_assumptions.rationale: Product choice: a 25-year projection with no discounting, the same horizon as the US and GB calculators. Inverter and battery replacement are not modelled.
Product choice: electricity prices flat (low), rising 2% a year (likely) or 4% a year (high). Not a forecast and not sourced; the same planning range as the GB calculator.

Product choice: one battery is modelled as 10 kWh of usable capacity, the size of the CHOICE price row used for the battery cost (10 kWh, AUD 7,000-11,000 after rebate). It sits inside the first rebate tier (0-14 kWh). Not a recommendation.

Product choice: install dates are offered only up to 30 Jun 2027. The federal battery rebate factors (6.8, then 5.7) and the regulated feed-in rates are sourced for that window; the 2027-28 feed-in rates are not published yet. The STC price after 2026 is not known either (the dollar value uses the mid-May 2026 spot price).
Input sanity limit for the monthly bill field, so a typing slip (an extra zero) is caught. Not sourced.
Product choice: below this a payback figure is not meaningful for a rooftop installation, so the calculator warns instead. Not sourced.
Product choice: where a source gives a likely value but no bounds, low and high are likely -/+ 15% and the result says they are estimated. Placeholder until bounds are sourced. Same as GB.

Derived from 12 PVGIS 5.3 runs (1 kWp, 35 degree tilt, 14% losses, PVGIS-ERA5), retrieved 2026-11-22, for Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane: yield facing east, west or the pole divided by yield facing the equator (north, aspect 180). THE KEY "north" HOLDS THE POLE-FACING (SOUTH-FACING) RATIO FOR AUSTRALIA, because the keys are shared with northern-hemisphere markets where the equator-facing side is south. East/west ratios: Sydney 0.814 / 0.742, Melbourne 0.801 / 0.787, Brisbane 0.837 / 0.825 (low = smallest, high = largest, likely = mean of the six = 0.801). Pole-facing: 0.500, 0.516, 0.567 (likely = mean = 0.528). Source: https://re.jrc.ec.europa.eu/api/v5_3/PVcalc (lat/lon of each city, peakpower=1, loss=14, angle=35, aspect=180/90/-90/0).
Product choice: 0.5% less output each year, a conventional planning figure for crystalline silicon panels (same as the GB calculator). Not sourced.

PVGIS system losses (the key keeps its legacy name). 14% is the PVGIS default system loss and what every yield figure on the site uses; 20% (some shade) and 30% (heavy shade) are product choices that step the loss up for partial and heavy shade. Not sourced.

NO PRIMARY SOURCE FOUND (an open item for the owner: a missing fact, not a null column, so the generated docs/TODO-VERIFY.md does not list it). The same deliberately wide product-choice ranges as the GB calculator: how much solar output is used at home rather than exported depends on when the household is at home. Replace with a measured source (for example the HTW Berlin Stromspeicher-Inspektion or a national study) when one is verified.
model_assumptions.unit: fraction of solar output used at home

model_assumptions.rationale: Product choice: the SolarQuotes price table used for pricing runs from 3 kW to 13 kW and the 5-10 kW rows set the range, so the suggested size is capped at 10 kW rather than priced outside the data. Not sourced.
Product choice: size the system to cover 80% to 100% of estimated annual usage, which gives the low and high ends of the suggested size range. Not sourced.
